text:
alex: Hey team — putting together a single canonical protocol for quantized benchmark runs (FP8 / INT8 / 4-bit / mixed). Wanted to capture kernel selection, batching heuristics, KV cache behavior, and calibration warmup so we get fair apples-to-apples numbers. Thoughts?

maria: +1. We desperately need a checklist. Right now people compare numbers with different tokenizers, warmups, and power caps.

cheng: Can we start with a minimal set of constraints: same model weights + same tokenizer + fixed random seed for sampling? Also call out deterministic vs nondet sampling.

alex: Agreed. My draft items: 1) model version hash, 2) tokenizer vocab & preproc flags, 3) seed, 4) input distribution (prompt lengths) 5) kernel config per layer (fp32 fallback allowed?), 6) power limit.

maria: For warmup I propose: run 1k tokens warmup or 2 minutes of sustained generation before measuring, whichever is longer. Reason: KV-cache lazy allocation + JIT/kernels need time to stabilize.

cheng: I prefer a steady-state check rather than fixed #tokens. Our shorter prompts reach steady throughput faster; longer-context tests take longer to fill KV. Suggested: measure latency over sliding 30s windows and start measurement when 3 consecutive windows are within 5% of median.

alex: That sounds good. Let's make it: warmup until steady-state per cheng's rule OR 1k tokens max, whichever comes first. Document this precisely so CI runs are reproducible.

ci-bot: CI note: benchmark runs should run on isolated node with no other user jobs, single process per GPU, CUDA profiler disabled unless explicitly capturing kernel traces.

maria: Power limits: use default datacenter TDP for the GPU vendor? In practice we currently run experiments at 240W (A100) and 400W (H100 SXM). But that biases throughput. I'd rather specify: record the power cap used and provide both capped and uncapped numbers.

alex: We'll require reporting the power cap as metadata. If comparing two kernels, they must be run under identical cap. Also include GPU clocks if pinned.

cheng: Kernel selection: document chosen kernel per op (attention, matmul, layernorm) + why (throughput vs numerical stability). If fallback to fp32 for some layers due to calibration, log which layers fell back.

maria: Calibration: for INT8/4-bit methods we must state calibration dataset and sampling method. Use a representative corpus of 5k prompts sampled from production distribution; include mean token length and stddev. Save seed. Also log scale ranges per tensor for post-calib methods.

alex: Good call. Also add a line: when running per-layer mixed precision, capture per-layer latency contribution and peak memory. That helps explain speed/quality tradeoffs.

dave: On batching heuristics: we need to freeze batch composition for fair runs. Options: 1) fixed micro-batch sizes with synthetic inter-arrival timings, 2) fixed single-stream inference. I vote for two canonical modes: single-stream low-latency (batch=1, no batching) and throughput mode (batching with controlled inter-arrival pattern).

cheng: For throughput mode, define inter-arrival using Poisson process with lambda set to target QPS or use replay traces from prod (preferred). Always report batch-size distribution and average tokens/batch.

maria: KV cache: differences in KV cache eviction/placement can change memory and latency. Protocol: 1) run with cold-cache baseline (start fresh) and 2) warm-cache steady-state (after warmup). Always snapshot cache hit ratio and effective sequence length.

alex: Add to that: when comparing quantized kernels, ensure KV caching format is identical (e.g., float16 vs int8-packed). If quantized kernels use packed KV encodings that change access patterns, call that out and include micro-benchmarks for KV read/write throughput.

dave: Example catch: we saw FP8 kernel gave 1.4x throughput but had 0.8 BLEU in downstream eval because calibration used different tokenization normalization. So: canonicalize tokenizer with NFKC/NFC and lowercasing flags recorded.

maria: Evaluation metrics: latency p50/p90/p99, throughput (tokens/s), tokens-per-dollar (if applicable), and a small quality suite (ROUGE/BLEU or log-likelihood delta) over the calibration+eval set. Report both absolute and delta vs fp32 baseline.

cheng: Logging: export per-step kernel names, durations, GPU utilization, mem footprint every 5s, and sample traces for when latency spikes > 2x baseline. Save raw profiler outputs as artifacts.

alex: One more thing: deterministic runs are preferred for regression checks, but for production-like benchmarks sample-based (top-k/top-p) configs should be included. Always log sampling temperature and top-k/p.

maria: Proposed final checklist (short):
- Model hash + tokenizer + seed
- Calibration dataset + sampling seed + per-tensor scale ranges
- Power cap + GPU clocks
- Warmup rule: steady-state windows or 1k tokens
- Modes: single-stream latency, throughput batching (with distribution)
- Kernel map + fallbacks + per-layer latencies
- KV cache cold + warm; cache hit rate + encoding format
- Metrics: p50/p90/p99, tokens/s, quality deltas, tokens-per-dollar
- Logs: kernel-level traces + profiler artifacts

alex: Ok I'll draft a canonical doc and CI job that enforces these. Can people review a rough draft by EOD? @maria @cheng @dave

maria: I'll review. Also add a short section with common pitfalls and quick reproduction commands (nvidia-smi commands, export env vars, example script to replay trace).

cheng: Will check kernel mapping section. We should also include a sample JSON schema for reporting results.

alex: Thanks — I'll push draft into /docs/benchmarks and add a small example run to CI.

ci-bot: Reminder: please attach the raw run artifact (.nvprof / tracy / perf) when merging benchmarks doc.

maria: Thanks all :thumbsup:
